name: Tunar Ahmadzada
tagline: 11th-grade researcher working at the intersection of artificial intelligence and computational mathematics
summary: 11th-grade student pursuing independent work at the intersection of artificial intelligence and computational mathematics. Selected as one of four students nationwide to represent Azerbaijan at the International Olympiad in Artificial Intelligence (IOAI), earning a Gold Medal at the National Round. Research in algorithmic number theory received national recognition at ISEF, while an applied computational project received NASA's Galactic Problem Solver award. Seeking to build on this research-driven foundation through rigorous undergraduate study in Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence.

projects.title: Common Divisibility Framework for Prime Numbers
projects.description: Researched divisibility properties of prime numbers and developed a single generalized algorithm capable of determining divisibility by any positive integer, unifying classical divisor-specific rules into one method. Presented at Azerbaijan's national ISEF qualifying round, earning a Bronze Medal in Mathematics against republic-level candidates.

projects.title: Space Debris Recycling System
projects.tag: NASA Space Apps Challenge — Global Hackathon
projects.description: Designed a device concept for the efficient, sustainable management of space debris, enabling in-orbit debris to be repurposed as raw material and 3D-printed on-site into spare parts needed for spacecraft and station maintenance. Built the computational solution within a 48-hour international hackathon, applying data analysis and rapid-prototyping methods to model the debris-to-part production workflow. Awarded the "Galactic Problem Solver" distinction.

experience.org: NASA Space Apps Challenge — Mingachevir, Azerbaijan
points: Lead the Mingachevir Local Event of the NASA International Space Apps Challenge, a global hackathon engaging 480,000+ participants across 190+ countries since 2012.
Direct the local chapter's two-day hackathon, coordinating outreach, mentorship, and judging with NASA's Global Organizing Team.
Co-founded and administer a nonprofit technology community offering free webinars, seminars, and problem-solving discussions to tech enthusiasts of all ages.
Run free, open-to-all competitions with prizes for community members.

experience.org: International Youth Math Challenge (IYMC) — Baku, Azerbaijan
points: Spearheaded local promotion and organized peer study groups, guiding participants through the Qualification and Pre-Final rounds of a competition spanning 100+ countries.
Evaluated mobile application submissions for a global entrepreneurship competition spanning 50+ countries; earned Technovation's Gold Certificate for excellence in evaluation and mentorship.
Represented Azerbaijan's National Team after earning a Gold Medal at the National Round; selected as 1 of 4 students nationwide to advance to the international round.
